extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, editors, and readers interested in Nature Communications' transparent peer review policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of Nature Communications' policy for publishing reviewer reports and author responses (transparent peer review), including who is involved, what is published, anonymity rules, and uptake metrics. Useful for authors deciding whether to opt in and for reviewers/editors understanding expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to publish reviewer reports and author rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Communications offers the option to publish the reviewer reports and author rebuttal letters for published papers submitted from January 2016 onwards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to opt in to this scheme upon acceptance of the paper. The published material comprises reviewer reports and author responses (peer review file) attached to the accepted manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-in at acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are asked to opt in to publishing the peer review history upon acceptance of their paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opt-in is voluntary; uptake is tracked by research area. The page reports an average opt-in rate of around 60% across the journal's content and variation by field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity maintained unless signed
rubrics_metrics.description: The anonymity of reviewers is maintained, unless they sign their reports to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may choose to sign their reports; if they do not sign, their confidentiality is preserved. This allows optional attribution while protecting anonymity by default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: increase transparency of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Intention is to open up the peer review process at the journal and to provide information on the expert reports that led to the editorial decision to publish a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer reports serve both as background on the merits of a study and to inform about the discussion between authors and reviewers; publishing these reports supports that goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of outputs covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal accepted manuscripts (and their associated peer review files) are the outputs for which review histories may be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy applies to published, accepted manuscripts submitted from the stated start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requested by
rubrics_metrics.description: Review requested by: Authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary indicates that reviews are requested in the context of author submissions (i.e., traditional journal submission flow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selected by: Editor, service, or community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of reviewers may be performed by the journal's professional editors, an external service, or community mechanisms depending on the workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interaction: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no public commenting or open public discussion during the review process for manuscripts under this policy; interaction is between reviewers, editors, and authors, with reports optionally published after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Author response: Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors provide rebuttal letters / responses to reviewer reports as part of the review record; these author responses can be included in the published peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision type
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision: Binary decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal's decision process is summarized as producing a binary decision (accept/reject) in the context reported here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Review coverage: Complete paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the entire manuscript rather than limited sections; the peer review history corresponds to full-paper review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity known to editors/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity known to: Editor or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewer identities are known to editors (or the service managing review), they are not disclosed to the public unless reviewers sign their reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests are checked
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing interests: Checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal checks for competing interests as part of the review process; this is part of quality and ethical screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript and review hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript hosting: Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review files (reviewer reports and author responses) are hosted along with the accepted manuscript on the journal platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible reviewers/editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional Editors invite reviewers to evaluate manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Communications uses professional editors to select and invite peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tags or badges for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Tags or badges: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary indicates there is no separate tag or badge system applied to papers to denote transparent peer review on this record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency attributes (open reports / blind types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency: Open reports; Single blind; Double blind (listed as transparency tags).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists multiple transparency-related tags: 'Open reports' (reports published), and blind review labels ('Single blind', 'Double blind') — the implementation preserves reviewer anonymity unless reviewers sign and supports published reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of outputs with review files
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of scholarly outputs commented on: 10,000+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the scale of published peer review files attached to manuscripts under this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric: author opt-in rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Metric tracked: Rate at which authors are opting in to the publication of the peer review files; author opt-in rate across different research areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to monitor adoption; the page reports around 60% average opt-in and field-by-field variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results summary / empirical uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: On average, around 60% of authors voluntarily opt in to publishing the peer review history of their paper; uptake varies by field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary commentary: uptake stronger where open peer review is commonplace and reviewers often sign; in some areas authors remain hesitant, but in almost all research areas the majority of published papers will contain a peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results URL / example implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Results URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms13626
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concrete publication/example demonstrating the journal's application of transparent peer review (peer review file available on article page).
